# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteNVMe: the configuration and MMIO accessors, the
I/O engine, the host-memory window, the request generator, the core control and the
root port configuration, with the registers of the LitePCIe PHY they work with. It is
generated from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated by the standalone
generator `litenvme/gen.py` on its example `examples/alibaba_xcku3p.yml` in its
benchmark variant, without running an FPGA toolchain or compiling the firmware.

Offsets are in bytes from the base of the bank; the base addresses depend on the SoC
and are in the `csr.csv` of a build. The bench SoC `bench/alibaba_xcku3p.py` wires
the blocks itself and gives them other names (`cfg_cfg_*`, `mmio_mem_*`,
`nvme_engine_engine_*`, `hostmem_csr_*`, `nvme_gen_*`), with the same registers in
each block.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `xcku3p_request_gen` | `litenvme_gen` `alibaba_xcku3p.yml` `with_block_streamer=False` `with_request_gen=True` `firmware=none` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The firmware and the host scripts of `bench/` use these names through the generated
`csr.h` and `csr.csv`, so they never need the offsets.

## Configuration accessor {#reg-nvme-cfg}

Defined by `LiteNVMePCIeCfgAccessor` (`litenvme/cfg.py`).

`LiteNVMe` collects its sub-blocks into one `nvme` bank, which this appendix splits per
sub-block, keeping the offsets from the base of `nvme` (full names such as
`nvme_cfg_cfg_ctrl`). The bank names given in this section and the next four
(`nvme_cfg`, `nvme_mmio`, `nvme_io_engine`, `nvme_hostmem`, `nvme_request_gen`) are
labels of these groups, not banks of `csr.csv`: add the offsets to the base of `nvme`.

Software sets `cfg_bdf` and, for a write, `cfg_wdata`, then writes `start` and polls
`cfg_stat` until `done` or `err` is set ([Configuration and register access](#pcie-access)).
The register reached is at byte `(ext << 6 | reg) * 4`, within the first 2 KiB of the
configuration space.

Bank `nvme_cfg`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `cfg_ctrl` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `cfg_bdf` | `0x0004` | 25 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `cfg_wdata` | `0x0008` | 32 | rw | CFG write data (DWORD). Reset `0x0`. |
| `cfg_stat` | `0x000c` | 2 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `cfg_rdata` | `0x0010` | 32 | ro | CFG read data (DWORD). |

Fields of `cfg_ctrl`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `start` | 0 | Write 1: send the configuration request (pulse). |
| `we` | 1 | 0: CfgRd0, 1: CfgWr0. |

Fields of `cfg_bdf`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `bus` | 7:0 | Bus number. |
| `dev` | 12:8 | Device number. |
| `fn` | 15:13 | Function number. |
| `reg` | 21:16 | DWORD register number (offset/4). |
| `ext` | 24:22 | Extended register number. |

Fields of `cfg_stat`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `done` | 0 | Transaction done. |
| `err` | 1 | Transaction error (completion error/timeout). |

## MMIO accessor {#reg-nvme-mmio}

Defined by `LiteNVMePCIeMmioAccessor` (`litenvme/mem.py`).

Registers of bank `nvme`, offsets from its base (`nvme_mmio_mem_*`).

The MMIO accessor reads and writes 32-bit registers of BAR0: software sets the 64-bit
byte address in `mem_adr_h` and `mem_adr_l`, `len` at 1 and, for a write, `mem_wdata`,
then writes `start` and polls `mem_stat`. Writes are posted. The I/O engine rings its
doorbells through a second MMIO accessor that has no registers.

Bank `nvme_mmio`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `mem_ctrl` | `0x0014` | 18 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `mem_adr_l` | `0x0018` | 32 | rw | MEM address low (bytes). Reset `0x0`. |
| `mem_adr_h` | `0x001c` | 32 | rw | MEM address high (bytes). Reset `0x0`. |
| `mem_wdata` | `0x0020` | 32 | rw | MEM write data (DWORD). Reset `0x0`. |
| `mem_stat` | `0x0024` | 2 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `mem_rdata` | `0x0028` | 32 | ro | MEM read data (DWORD). |

Fields of `mem_ctrl`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `start` | 0 | Write 1: send the memory request (pulse). |
| `we` | 1 | 0: MemRd, 1: MemWr (posted). |
| `wsel` | 7:4 | Byte enables of a write; only `0xf` is accepted, another value ends the request with `err`. |
| `len` | 17:8 | DWORD count (start with 1). |

Fields of `mem_stat`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `done` | 0 | Transaction done. |
| `err` | 1 | Transaction error (completion error/timeout/invalid wsel). |

## I/O engine {#reg-nvme-io-engine}

Defined by `LiteNVMeIOEngine` (`litenvme/io_engine.py`).

Registers of bank `nvme`, offsets from its base (`nvme_io_engine_*`).

Software programs the queue bases (host-memory window addresses), the doorbell
addresses (BAR0 byte addresses) and the PRP-list region, then sets `enable`
([The I/O engine](#io-engine)).

Bank `nvme_io_engine`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `engine_enable` | `0x002c` | 1 | rw | Enable the hardware I/O engine. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_sq_base_` `lo` | `0x0030` | 32 | rw | IO SQ base (host byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_sq_base_` `hi` | `0x0034` | 32 | rw | IO SQ base (host byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_cq_base_` `lo` | `0x0038` | 32 | rw | IO CQ base (host byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_cq_base_` `hi` | `0x003c` | 32 | rw | IO CQ base (host byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_sq_db_lo` | `0x0040` | 32 | rw | SQ doorbell (BAR0 byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_sq_db_hi` | `0x0044` | 32 | rw | SQ doorbell (BAR0 byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_cq_db_lo` | `0x0048` | 32 | rw | CQ doorbell (BAR0 byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_cq_db_hi` | `0x004c` | 32 | rw | CQ doorbell (BAR0 byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_prp_` `list_lo` | `0x0050` | 32 | rw | PRP-list region (host byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_prp_` `list_hi` | `0x0054` | 32 | rw | PRP-list region (host byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `engine_status` | `0x0058` | 16 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `engine_` `submitted` | `0x005c` | 32 | ro | Total commands submitted. |
| `engine_` `completed` | `0x0060` | 32 | ro | Total completions reaped. |

Fields of `engine_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `busy` | 0 | 1: the engine FSM is not idle. |
| `inflight` | 15:8 | Commands submitted and not yet reaped. |

## Host-memory window {#reg-nvme-hostmem}

Defined by `LiteNVMeHostMemCSR` (`litenvme/hostmem.py`).

Registers of bank `nvme`, offsets from its base (`nvme_hostmem_csr_*`).

Present with `with_hostmem_csr`, which the generator turns off when the block streamer
is the sole front-end. `csr_adr` is a dword index from the base of the window; the
read path uses a third port of the window memory. `csr_we` is a level: the firmware
writes 1 then 0, and the write repeats while it stays at 1 (one dword written with
byte enables each time).

The counters observe the PCIe side
of the window. `rd_gap_max` counts from reset, so it is meaningful only after the
first beat ([The host-memory window](#host-memory)).

Bank `nvme_hostmem`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `csr_csr_adr` | `0x0064` | 32 | rw | HostMem dword address (index). Reset `0x0`. |
| `csr_csr_wdata` | `0x0068` | 32 | rw | HostMem write data (DWORD). Reset `0x0`. |
| `csr_csr_we` | `0x006c` | 1 | rw | HostMem write request (level: write 1 then 0). Reset `0x0`. |
| `csr_csr_rdata` | `0x0070` | 32 | ro | HostMem read data (DWORD). |
| `csr_dma_wr_` `count` | `0x0074` | 32 | ro | Count of DMA beats stored. |
| `csr_dma_rd_` `count` | `0x0078` | 32 | ro | Count of DMA beats served. |
| `csr_wr_present_` `cycles` | `0x007c` | 32 | ro | Cycles a MemWr beat is offered at the port. |
| `csr_wr_accept_` `cycles` | `0x0080` | 32 | ro | Cycles a MemWr beat is accepted. |
| `csr_wr_stall_` `cycles` | `0x0084` | 32 | ro | Cycles a MemWr beat is offered but backpressured. |
| `csr_rd_tlp_` `count` | `0x0088` | 32 | ro | Number of read-completion (MemWr) TLPs accepted. |
| `csr_rd_gap_max` | `0x008c` | 32 | ro | Longest idle run (cycles) between offered MemWr beats. |

## Request generator {#reg-nvme-request-gen}

Defined by `LiteNVMeRequestGen` (`litenvme/request_gen.py`).

Registers of bank `nvme`, offsets from its base (`nvme_request_gen_*`).

Present with `with_request_gen`. The generator issues `count` commands at
`base_lba + k * lba_step`, with the buffer `buf_base + (k % qmod) * buf_stride`
([Front-ends](#frontends)). The block streamer also has a register wrapper
(`sector`, `count`, `nsid`, `ctrl`, `status`, `cycles`, in `litenvme/block.py`), which
the generator does not build: it exposes the block streamer on pins.

Bank `nvme_request_gen`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `op` | `0x0090` | 1 | rw | 0=read, 1=write. Reset `0x0`. |
| `nsid` | `0x0094` | 32 | rw | Namespace ID. Reset `0x0`. |
| `base_lba_lo` | `0x0098` | 32 | rw | Base LBA low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `base_lba_hi` | `0x009c` | 32 | rw | Base LBA high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `nlb` | `0x00a0` | 16 | rw | Blocks per command (1-based). Reset `0x1`. |
| `lba_step` | `0x00a4` | 32 | rw | LBA increment between commands. Reset `0x0`. |
| `count` | `0x00a8` | 32 | rw | Number of commands to issue. Reset `0x1`. |
| `buf_base_lo` | `0x00ac` | 32 | rw | PRP1 buffer base (host byte addr) low. Reset `0x0`. |
| `buf_base_hi` | `0x00b0` | 32 | rw | PRP1 buffer base (host byte addr) high. Reset `0x0`. |
| `buf_stride` | `0x00b4` | 32 | rw | Per-slot buffer stride (bytes). Reset `0x1000`. |
| `qmod` | `0x00b8` | 16 | rw | Buffer-key modulus (== engine qsize). Reset `0x40`. |
| `ctrl` | `0x00bc` | 1 | rw | Start the run. Reset `0x0`. |
| `status` | `0x00c0` | 1 | ro | Run complete / idle. |
| `completed` | `0x00c4` | 32 | ro | Completions counted. |
| `errors` | `0x00c8` | 32 | ro | Completions with error status. |
| `cycles` | `0x00cc` | 32 | ro | Cycles from start to last completion. |
| `last_status` | `0x00d0` | 16 | ro | Last CQE status field. |
| `first_err_` `status` | `0x00d4` | 16 | ro | Status of the first erroring CQE. |
| `first_err_cid` | `0x00d8` | 16 | ro | CID of the first erroring CQE. |
| `first_err_idx` | `0x00dc` | 32 | ro | Completion index of the first error. |

## Core control {#reg-nvme-ctrl}

Defined by `LiteNVMeCoreControl` (`litenvme/core.py`).

Present with `init_mode` `firmware`. With `rtl`, the init sequencer drives the status
pins and this bank does not exist ([Bring-up](#bringup)).

Bank `nvme_ctrl`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `init_done` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | Written to 1 by the bring-up firmware when the controller and the I/O queue are ready; drives `status_init_done` of the standalone core. Reset `0x0`. |
| `init_error` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | Written to 1 by the bring-up firmware when the bring-up failed; drives `status_init_error`. Reset `0x0`. |

## Root port configuration {#reg-pcie-rootcfg}

Defined by `LiteNVMeRootCfgMgmt` (`litenvme/cfg.py`).

Reaches the configuration space of the root port itself through the `cfg_mgmt` port of
the hard IP (dword address), with a handshake to the `pcie` clock domain. The firmware
uses it to raise the Max Payload Size of the root port and to program its memory
window. Present with `init_mode` `firmware`.

Bank `pcie_rootcfg`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `ctrl` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `addr` | `0x0004` | 10 | rw | DWORD address into Root Port config space. Reset `0x0`. |
| `func` | `0x0008` | 8 | rw | Function number (0 for PF0). Reset `0x0`. |
| `wdata` | `0x000c` | 32 | rw | Write data (DWORD). Reset `0x0`. |
| `be` | `0x0010` | 4 | rw | Byte enables. Reset `0xf`. |
| `stat` | `0x0014` | 2 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `rdata` | `0x0018` | 32 | ro | Read data (valid when done=1). |

Fields of `ctrl`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `start` | 0 | Start a cfg_mgmt transaction. |
| `write` | 1 | 0=Read, 1=Write. |

Fields of `stat`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `done` | 0 | Last transaction complete. |
| `busy` | 1 | Transaction in progress. |

## PCIe PHY (LitePCIe) {#reg-pcie-phy}

Defined by `USPPCIEPHY` (`litepcie/phy/usppciephy.py`).

Registers of the LitePCIe PHY, documented in the LitePCIe manual. `link_status` is the
first register to read on a new bench ([Debugging](#debugging)).

Bank `pcie_phy`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `link_status` | `0x0000` | 15 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `msi_enable` | `0x0004` | 1 | ro | MSI Enable Status. ``1``: MSI is enabled. |
| `bus_master_` `enable` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | Bus Mastering Status. ``1``: Bus Mastering enabled. |
| `max_request_` `size` | `0x000c` | 16 | ro | Negiotiated Max Request Size (in bytes). |
| `max_payload_` `size` | `0x0010` | 16 | ro | Negiotiated Max Payload Size (in bytes). |

Fields of `link_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `status` | 0 | 1: link up. |
| `phy_down` | 1 | 1: PHY link down. |
| `phy_status` | 3:2 | 0: no receiver detected, 1: training, 2: link up and data link initialization in progress, 3: link up, data link initialized. |
| `rate` | 5:4 | 0: 2.5 GT/s (Gen1), 1: 5.0 GT/s (Gen2), 2: 8.0 GT/s (Gen3). |
| `width` | 8:6 | 0: x1, 1: x2, 2: x4, 3: x8, 4: x16. |
| `ltssm` | 14:9 | LTSSM State |
